model_metadata:
### Model stg_orders
File: models/staging/stg_orders.sql · materialized as view
Description: Cleaned orders, one row per order. Expected volume is 500-1,000 orders over the 180-day window.
Columns (name · type in warehouse · description · tests):
- order_id · INTEGER · Primary key of the order. · tests: unique, not_null
- customer_id · INTEGER · Customer who placed the order (foreign key to stg_customers). · tests: not_null
- order_date · DATE · Date the order was placed. · tests: not_null
- status · VARCHAR · Order lifecycle status. · tests: accepted_values(values=['placed', 'shipped', 'completed', 'cancelled'])
- loaded_at · TIMESTAMP · UTC timestamp when the row was loaded into the warehouse.
Model-level tests: row_count_between(min_rows=500, max_rows=1000)
SQL (models/staging/stg_orders.sql):
```sql
with source as (

    select * from {{ source('raw', 'raw_orders') }}

),

renamed as (

    select
        order_id,
        customer_id,
        cast(order_date as date) as order_date,
        status,
        loaded_at
    from source

)

select * from renamed
```

### Model stg_payments
File: models/staging/stg_payments.sql · materialized as view
Description: Cleaned payments, one row per payment. Amount converted from cents to currency units.
Columns (name · type in warehouse · description · tests):
- payment_id · INTEGER · Primary key of the payment. · tests: unique, not_null
- order_id · INTEGER · Order the payment belongs to (foreign key to stg_orders). · tests: not_null, relationships(to=stg_orders, field=order_id)
- payment_method · VARCHAR · Payment method used. · tests: accepted_values(values=['credit_card', 'bank_transfer', 'voucher', 'gift_card'])
- amount · DOUBLE · Payment amount in currency units (raw cents / 100). · tests: not_null
- loaded_at · TIMESTAMP · UTC timestamp when the row was loaded into the warehouse.
SQL (models/staging/stg_payments.sql):
```sql
with source as (

    select * from {{ source('raw', 'raw_payments') }}

),

renamed as (

    select
        payment_id,
        order_id,
        payment_method,
        -- source stores integer cents; convert to currency units
        cast(amount as decimal(18, 2)) / 100 as amount,
        loaded_at
    from source

)

select * from renamed
```

Upstream nodes and their current warehouse columns:
- source raw.raw_orders (source table): order_id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, order_date DATE, status VARCHAR, loaded_at TIMESTAMP
- source raw.raw_payments (source table): payment_id INTEGER, order_id INTEGER, payment_method VARCHAR, amount INTEGER, loaded_at TIMESTAMP
Downstream nodes (affected if the failing node is wrong or skipped):
- model dim_customers (table): One row per customer with order history and lifetime value. Used by marketing and finance dashboards.
- model fct_orders (table): One row per order with payment amounts pivoted by method. Grain must match stg_orders (one row per order).
- exposure finance_revenue_dashboard (dashboard, owner: Finance analytics): Daily revenue by payment method and order status. Refreshed at 07:00 UTC and used in the daily finance stand-up.
- exposure marketing_customer_dashboard (dashboard, owner: Marketing analytics): Customer counts, lifetime value and repeat-purchase rate by country.
Column-level lineage (as designed):
- stg_orders.{order_id, customer_id, status, loaded_at} ← raw_orders (same names)
- stg_orders.order_date ← raw_orders.order_date (cast to date)
- stg_payments.{payment_id, order_id, payment_method, loaded_at} ← raw_payments (same names)
- stg_payments.amount ← raw_payments.amount (integer cents / 100)

- dim_customers.{first_order_date, most_recent_order_date, number_of_orders} ← stg_orders.order_date / order_id, per customer_id
- dim_customers.lifetime_value ← stg_payments.amount joined via stg_orders.order_id, non-cancelled orders, per customer_id
- fct_orders.{order_id, customer_id, order_date, status} ← stg_orders (same names)
- fct_orders.{credit_card_amount, bank_transfer_amount, voucher_amount, gift_card_amount} ← stg_payments.amount by payment_method, per order_id
- fct_orders.amount ← stg_payments.amount, total per order_id
historical_context:
Recent changes (newest first):
- 2026-10-13 · commit 12cac3c · ingestion-config repo: set orders extract `lookback_days: 60` to speed up hourly loads (PR #88)
- 2026-10-08 · ticket · BI-204: 'Weekly revenue' tile added to the finance revenue dashboard (reads fct_orders)
- 2026-10-04 · commit cf1ac3f · docs: add column descriptions to models/marts/schema.yml (no SQL change)
Previous incidents:
- INC-0320 (2026-07-10): payments extract missed one hour after a connector restart. Resolution: hour re-extracted.
Recent run history:
- stg_orders row count, last 7 daily runs: 584, 587, 590, 594, 594, 597, 209 today (2026-10-13).
- raw_payments row count: stable (636 today).

gold_standard_remediation.root_cause: raw.raw_orders now holds only 209 orders, all with order_date on or after 2026-08-14. That is exactly a 60-day window, set this morning by PR #88 (`lookback_days: 60`). The orders load replaces the table, so all older orders disappeared. stg_orders falls below the 500-row minimum. Payments still cover the full history, so 415 payments now reference missing orders and the relationships test on stg_payments.order_id fails too.
gold_standard_remediation.fix: Revert PR #88, or switch the orders load to incremental merge on order_id so a short lookback no longer deletes history. Then run a one-off full-history extract to restore raw_orders and re-run `dbt build`. Do not lower the row-count threshold or remove the relationships test: both caught a real data loss.
gold_standard_remediation.verification: `select count(*), min(order_date) from raw.raw_orders` returns about 600 rows, starting about 180 days ago. `dbt build --select stg_orders+` passes, including the relationships test on stg_payments.order_id.
gold_standard_remediation.text:
Root cause: raw.raw_orders now holds only 209 orders, all with order_date on or after 2026-08-14. That is exactly a 60-day window, set this morning by PR #88 (`lookback_days: 60`). The orders load replaces the table, so all older orders disappeared. stg_orders falls below the 500-row minimum. Payments still cover the full history, so 415 payments now reference missing orders and the relationships test on stg_payments.order_id fails too.

Fix: Revert PR #88, or switch the orders load to incremental merge on order_id so a short lookback no longer deletes history. Then run a one-off full-history extract to restore raw_orders and re-run `dbt build`. Do not lower the row-count threshold or remove the relationships test: both caught a real data loss.

Verification: `select count(*), min(order_date) from raw.raw_orders` returns about 600 rows, starting about 180 days ago. `dbt build --select stg_orders+` passes, including the relationships test on stg_payments.order_id.
